title: Self-Improving Language Models for Evolutionary Program Synthesis: A Case Study on ARC-AGI
summary: The pinned greedy-diverse selector has an empty-dictionary invariant that removes the intended low-performing diversity half. Main-text, appendix and released voting rules are non-equivalent and can select different top-two output patterns. Exact equal-compute matching remains Needs Evidence. Historical benchmark damage and hidden-answer leakage are not established.
limitations: No author-code execution, model loading, installation or empirical benchmark reproduction.
Source-only snapshot omits binary few-shot archive, model weights and historical search/training traces; omission is not proof authors never released them.
Historical producing commit/configuration not established; findings do not prove reported benchmark score damage.
Validation label-use checks cover inspected paths only, not every preprocessing option or historical archive.
Separate supplement availability unknown after OpenReview metadata403.
Later external state-of-the-art claims and all cited works not independently verified.

problems.title: Pinned greedy-diverse selector drops the entire intended diversity half

source_claim.paraphrase: The core greedy-diverse dataset selects up to25 high-performing and25 low-performing candidates per task; the released default implements that selection.

assumptions: Ordinary finite well-formed candidate records reach the selected helper
The pinned source uses an initially empty dictionary whose sole write is guarded by preexisting key membership
Historical producing revision is not established
problems.check: Text-only AST inspection verifies empty initialization, sole subscript write inside membership-true branch and no alternative insertion. By induction the dictionary remains empty for every candidate. The residual pool is empty, all three diverse-selection passes add zero and the default output has at most25 greedy plus0 diverse examples. A pool with25 eligible high and25 distinct eligible low candidates still loses all intended low candidates.
problems.result: The pinned default cannot implement the claimed greedy-diverse data construction; no author function was executed.
counterevidence: Historical experiments may have used a different revision.
Remaining greedy examples may still be failed on the original task and support hindsight learning.
Refinement training remains a separate data path.
No benchmark deterioration or collapse of the whole self-improvement method is established.
problems.core_dependency: Diverse low-performing program traces are central to the data-selection ablation and explanation for sustained self-improvement.
problems.impact: Major scoped implementation failure of a central contribution and its reproducibility link; no numerical score loss is asserted.

correction.statement: Insert unseen keys with an explicit representative policy and verify survival/count of eligible unique residual candidates. Original source preserved; no patch, author-code execution or historical rerun.

problems.title: Core weighted-voting prescriptions select different top-two outputs

source_claim.paraphrase: Output voting aggregates visible-example accuracy to choose submitted patterns and to weight test-time data groups.

assumptions: GroupA has10 programs with accuracy.2; B has1 with accuracy1; C has1 with accuracy.8
Five visible examples permit these accuracies
No ties and no hidden labels are involved

Appendix train_accuracy is defined per generated program over visible examples; aggregation across programs in one pattern is not specified. Each witness group is homogeneous, so mean and representative-program readings agree.
problems.check: Main sum gives A2,B1,C.8. The literal appendix count+1000accuracy, using the common within-group program accuracy, gives A210,B1001,C801. Release sum(1+1000accuracy) gives A2010,B1001,C801. Top two are A,B for main/release versus B,C for the literal appendix reading. The witness does not require averaging unequal-accuracy programs. Main and release are not exactly equivalent either because release adds counts.
problems.result: The written pseudocode and pinned release can implement different evaluation and adaptation decisions.
counterevidence: An intended sum across programs, or an omitted count multiplier, could reconcile the appendix with the release; the original does not specify that group aggregation.
Release is closer to the main-text weighted-frequency description.
Both aggregators can be legitimate heuristics and agree in special cases.
No actual historical prediction or score change was established.
problems.core_dependency: Voting determines submitted output patterns and test-time data selection weights, both core pipeline steps.
problems.impact: Major core algorithm-specification discrepancy, demonstrated by a changed top-two set; historical numerical impact remains unknown.

correction.statement: Specify exact group-weight formula, count term, grouping, tie rule and scorer revision. Connect to archived search outputs before claiming numerical impact.

problems.title: Equal-compute comparison needs actual training and search accounting

source_claim.paraphrase: Finetuning is about5percent of computation and a12600-attempt fixed-model search matches one improvement cycle with two6000-attempt searches plus training.

assumptions: Conditional diagnostic adopts paper dense coefficients6N for training and2N for generation
D selected examples per task, e epochs
D100 is an upper value, not measured historical count; e3 is stated/default
problems.check: Training/search6000 ratio=3eD/6000. AtD100,e3 training equals900 generation attempts,15percent of one search or7.5percent of two, total12900. AtD=200/3 the same simplified accounting gives600, so discrepancy alone does not establish actual FLOPs.
problems.result: Exact cost matching cannot be verified from nominal attempts and incomplete token/example counts.
counterevidence: At most100 examples need not mean100 actually used.
LoRA/QLoRA costs differ from dense coefficients.
Prompt/response lengths, caching and early stopping affect actual computation.
Problem1 must not be used to infer historical dataset size.
No conclusion that corrected fixed-model search catches SOAR.
problems.core_dependency: The specific claim that performance improvements survive an equal-compute search comparison.
problems.impact: Needs Evidence for exact FLOP matching; does not refute nominal-budget reported gains.

correction.statement: Supply producing configurations, selected example counts, epochs, per-stage token counts, adapter-training cost convention, cache/early-stop accounting and cumulative compute across iterations/models.
